title: Tight Security Bounds for XOCB
summary: For constant maximum input length, XOCB has a known bound of 2 to the power 2n/3 but an attack near 2 to the power n; tight bounds there and in the intermediate regime remain open.

formal_statement.body: XOCB is a beyond-birthday-bound secure authenticated-encryption mode with rate-one computation. For constant maximum input length $l = O(1)$, the known security bound is $2^{2n/3}$, whereas the relevant attack has complexity about $2^n$ queries and total processed data, so the bound is not known to be tight in this regime. More generally, the bound is also non-tight in the intermediate regime $O(1) < l < 2^{n/2}$. The unresolved task is to characterize the tight security bound for XOCB when $l$ is constant and, more generally, throughout that intermediate range of maximum input length.

scope.domain: Security-bound tightness for the XOCB rate-one authenticated-encryption mode.
parameters: n: exponent parameter governing the stated security bound and attack complexity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the tight XOCB security bound for constant maximum input length and throughout the intermediate range.

citations.label: XOCB: Beyond-Birthday-Bound Secure Authenticated Encryption Mode with Rate-One Computation

progress.summary: The paper contrasts the known bound for constant maximum input length with a much larger attack complexity and explicitly leaves further analysis open. It also presents the intermediate-length regime as non-tight.
citation_labels: Zhenzhen Bao et al., XOCB: Beyond-Birthday-Bound Secure Authenticated Encryption Mode with Rate-One Computation
